text:
alex: heads up — found a client hitting our /v1/generate with no Authorization but they do send `X-Project-ID`. behavior?
maria: should treat as unauthenticated unless API key present. X-Project-ID alone can't be used to identify owner.
jamal: is there any historical fallback where we used project header + ip allowlist?
maria: not in mainline. there was a one-off proxy hack last year but not supported by API. we return 401 currently.
ingrid: double-checking: does 401 vs 403 depend on missing vs invalid key in our contract? iirc missing -> 401, invalid -> 403.
alex: yep that's what our openapi example states. can we confirm code paths? pinging @deploy-bot for recent auth middleware deploys.
deploy-bot: deploy:auth-middleware v2.14 rolled at 2024-06-03 18:12 UTC — no auth header behavior unchanged (401 for missing). :rocket:
jamal: ok good. client says they rely on X-Project-ID to route requests to org-scoped billing. we need to explain why that can't be used as auth.
maria: short rationale to give them: headers are not secretable credentials, can be spoofed. billing routing needs authenticated key so we can tie usage to an account and enforce org-level quotas.
ingrid: can we offer a migration suggestion: accept X-Project-ID when paired with a signed HMAC header? maybe short-term compatibility shim.
maria: we have a safety policy that any new auth method requires audit logs + opt-in per org (security reasons). HMAC shim would be possible but needs product signoff.
ajmal: small ask: could middleware emit telemetry tag when X-Project-ID present but Authorization missing? would help support triage.
maria: good idea — log auth_hint:project_header_present = true. low cardinality, safe. i'll add to telemetry PR.
alex: also note: key rotation window question — if a client rotates keys and sends old key with X-Project-ID, we should return 403 not 401, correct?
ingrid: old key -> 403, because credential was presented but invalid. missing key -> 401.
jamal: for docs: add a tiny example showing curl w/ and w/o Authorization and expected responses.
alex: draft snippet i used for repro: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Project-ID: proj_abc" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
returns 401. with `-H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."` returns 200.
maria: i'll open a quick PR to add telemetry + small docs blurb. tagging for review: @jamal @ingrid.
jamal: lgtm for telemetry change, can review PR later today.
ingrid: i'll help write the docs example and call out why header is insufficient.
alex: thanks all. i'll reply to the customer with the explanation and short migration path (use key or contact sales for org-level routing options). :thumbsup:
